articles.title: Sonay Kartal: New British number one makes rapid rise after a slow recovery from back injury
articles.summary: Six months ago, Sonay Kartal could not brush her teeth without "being in agony" - now she's the British number one after three events back from a long-term back injury.
articles.body:
Six months ago, Sonay Kartal could not stand up and brush her teeth without "being in agony".

The pain caused by a stress fracture in her back eventually subsided, but the 24-year-old Briton still had a long road to full recovery, which needed to be navigated with patience and hard work.

Kartal did not make her return to competitive action until little under a month ago.

But on Monday, she became the new British number one after an extraordinary week at the Wuhan Open, where she reached the biggest final of her career in just her third tournament back.

"In the first month or so, I was at home in bed - sometimes I had good days but there were also bad days where I wasn't really able to walk without some form of pain," Kartal said.

"It was a slow process and it makes you think you do take every day things for granted a bit."

Given where Kartal was six months ago, and the length of time she was out injured, reaching the Wuhan final cannot be overstated as an achievement.

As a WTA 1,000 event, it is in the tier of tournaments directly below the Grand Slams and attracts the strongest fields on the women's tour.

Kartal knocked out a series of opponents with considerable pedigree - including current top-10 players and former Grand Slam champions - before running out of steam against this year's French Open runner-up Maja Chwalinska.

Falling to a brutal defeat from a set and break up in the final will undoubtedly sting. Kartal, though, quickly acknowledged the bigger picture is already more positive than she could have predicted.

Kartal was ranked 54th in the world when the back issue struck at Indian Wells in March and she used a protected injury ranking - given to players who have been out for six months or more - to compete in Wuhan.

Earning 650 points as the runner-up saw Kartal's ranking rocket from 170th to 49th - and now closing in on a career-high of 44th achieved in July 2025 after reaching the last 16 at Wimbledon.

And it is an example of the WTA's special ranking rule working as it is intended: providing a fair platform for a player to re-establish her position after a prolonged and unavoidable absence.

Regaining her ranking just 10 matches into her comeback will have real significance for the 2027 season.

Kartal will no longer need to use a protected ranking to enter tournaments including the Australian Open, meaning she can have greater choice over when and where to play as she continues to manage her workload.

On Monday, she pulled out of the Japan Open in Osaka, where she was due to play her first-round match on Tuesday.

"My goal on the Asian swing was just to try to defend those points I had from last year and make the use of the protected ranking worthwhile," said Kartal, who also won two matches at the China Open in Beijing.

"I think I've gone above and beyond that. The goal has been achieved this week and I'm in a good spot for the rest of the year and next year."

Kartal's re-emergence is timely too when considering the bigger picture of British success at the highest level.

With Kartal absent from three of the four majors, no British women went past the second round of a Grand Slam tournament in 2026.

Kartal has only managed to do that twice in her career - reaching the third round at Wimbledon in 2024 and going one stage further last year - but showed in Wuhan she has the ability to thrive at elite level.

She became the first British player to reach a WTA 1000 final since Johanna Konta in 2019 and, despite losing to 22nd-ranked Chwalinska, still recorded the best result by a British woman since Emma Raducanu won the US Open title in 2021.

Alongside Arthur Fery's extraordinary run to the Wimbledon semi-finals in the summer, it is a much-needed bright spot for the nation's tennis fans.

Similarly to Fery, she is not blessed with the height and power which many of the leading players on both tours are genetically given, but she certainly has enough damaging tools which can help anchor her inside the top 50.

In Wuhan, her consistent hitting from the baseline, supreme athleticism and level-headedness were the keys to her success.

Staying fit over the coming months will be another important factor.

Kartal says the stress fracture in her back has completely healed and her team say she "worked her socks off, 9-5 all the time" during rehabilitation to ensure she could hit the ground running when she did return.

It was telling that Kartal quickly paid tribute to her coach Ben Reeves, fitness coach Ian Aylward and physio Dani Gillanders after collecting the runners-up trophy.

"If it wasn't for them I wouldn't be here," Kartal said.

"It makes it even better that the three people who helped me get back to fitness and fixed my back are with me. It's been a special week for all of us."

articles.title: Rafa Jódar se sitúa noveno del año y se acerca a las ATP Finals de Turín
articles.standfirst: El madrileño le saca 279 puntos a De Miñaur, que ahora mismo sería el primer reserva
articles.summary: El madrileño le saca 279 puntos a De Miñaur, que ahora mismo sería el primer reserva
articles.body: El tenis masculino español puede clasificar a dos españoles en las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre). A Carlos Alcaraz, que ya tiene el billete, se le puede unir su compatriota Rafa Jódar. El madrileño ha ganado dos posiciones, gracias a la final del Masters 1000 de Shanghái, y se sitúa este lunes noveno de la Race 2026. Los 3.159 puntos le dejan a 166 de la octava plaza, que ahora mismo ocupa Arthur Fils, y le distancian de Alex de Miñaur en 279 puntos. El australiano es hoy el primer reserva de la cita de maestros. Novak Djokovic se queda a 319 puntos del fenómeno de Leganés. Es por ello que ha aceptado una invitación para participar en el Open 500 de Basilea. Rafa y el serbio coincidirán en tierras suizas. Jódar se ha quedado a tan sólo 91 puntos de convertirse en el vigésimo miembro de la 'Armada' en ingresar en las diez primeras posiciones del ranking de entradas de la ATP. En el Open 500 de Basilea (26 de octubre al 1 de noviembre) volverá a tener la oportunidad de ser el tercer español más precoz en conseguirlo tras Rafa Nadal y Carlos Alcaraz. Alejandro Davidovich, flamante campeón de Shanghái, es hoy el decimocuarto tenista del año y se ha metido en la carrera por estar en Turín. Le separan 649 puntos y quedan por disputarse 1.500 (Basilea y el Masters 1000 de París).

articles.title: Svitolina anuncia su separación de Monfils: "Nuestro matrimonio termina, pero nuestra familia no"
articles.standfirst: La tenista ucraniana explica el impacto emocional de la guerra y agradece el apoyo del francés: "Nunca me soltó la mano"
articles.summary: La tenista ucraniana explica el impacto emocional de la guerra y agradece el apoyo del francés: "Nunca me soltó la mano"
articles.body: Elina Svitolina ha anunciado el final de su matrimonio con Gaël Monfils a través de un comunicado en Instagram en el que explica el difícil momento personal que atraviesa. La ucraniana habla del sufrimiento que le ha provocado la guerra en su país y de una decisión dolorosa: "Necesito reencontrarme conmigo misma y no puedo hacerlo dentro de nuestro matrimonio". "Esto es lo más difícil que he tenido que compartir", comienza el mensaje. Svitolina recuerda que el año pasado explicó que necesitaba alejarse de las pistas porque no se encontraba en condiciones emocionales de competir. Ahora ha querido contar qué había detrás: "Lo que no visteis fueron las noches sin dormir, las dudas y la sensación de estar perdiéndome poco a poco". La tenista destaca el apoyo de Monfils durante todo ese proceso. "Gaël lo vio todo. Nunca me soltó la mano. Luchamos juntos durante mucho tiempo, con todo lo que teníamos", explica. Pero también expresa los límites de esa ayuda: "Algunas batallas se libran en lo más profundo de una misma y ningún amor de otra persona puede ganarlas por ti". Svitolina asegura que comprender lo que necesitaba y trasladárselo a su marido ha sido especialmente duro. "Es la verdad más difícil que he tenido que afrontar y lo más difícil que he tenido que decirle a la persona que amo". Del francés destaca su respuesta: "Ha respetado lo que necesito con una fortaleza y una elegancia que nunca olvidaré". El comunicado está atravesado por el cariño y el agradecimiento hacia quien ha compartido sus mejores y peores momentos. "Gaël me ha querido en mis mayores alegrías y en mis momentos más oscuros, y yo lo he querido con todo mi corazón", escribe. Por encima de la separación queda su hija Skai, a quien sitúa en el centro de esta nueva etapa. "Skai siempre será lo primero. Nuestro matrimonio termina, pero nuestra familia no. Siempre seremos sus padres, juntos, en cada paso de su vida". Svitolina cierra el anuncio con una petición de respeto para ambos y sin señalar culpables: "Solo hay dos personas que se han querido profundamente y una historia que está cambiando de forma". Y solicita comprensión y privacidad: "Os pedimos amabilidad y el espacio que necesitamos para sanar".

articles.title: Elina Svitolina announces split from Gael Monfils: ‘Our marriage is ending, but our family is not’
articles.summary: Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced the end of her marriage to French tennis player Gael Monfils, describing the decision as the most
articles.body: Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced the end of her marriage to French tennis player Gael Monfils, describing the decision as the most difficult thing she has ever had to share and opening up about the emotional struggles that shaped her journey over the past year.The world No. 6 made the announcement in an emotional Instagram post on Monday, explaining that she needed to rediscover herself after battling the psychological toll of the war in Ukraine. The couple, who have a daughter, Skai, together, said their family would remain united despite the end of their marriage.“This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share,” Svitolina wrote.The 32-year-old revealed that she had rarely spoken publicly about her inner struggles but had reached a point where she needed to step away from tennis to recover emotionally. She described sleepless nights, doubts and a feeling of losing herself during a particularly difficult period.‘No amount of love from someone else can win them for you’Svitolina acknowledged the role Monfils played in supporting her through her struggles, saying the Frenchman stood by her during some of the darkest moments of her life.“Gaël saw all of this. He never let go of my hand. We fought through it together for a long time, giving it all our strength,” she wrote.However, the Ukrainian explained that the emotional battles she was facing ultimately required a personal journey that she felt she could not undertake within their marriage.“But some battles happen deep inside you, and no amount of love from someone else can win them for you,” she wrote.“With time, I came to understand that I need to find my way back to myself and that I cannot do that within our marriage.”Svitolina described the decision as an extremely painful one, particularly because of the love and support she had shared with Monfils.“This is the hardest truth I have ever had to face and the hardest thing I have ever had to say to the person I love,” she said.She also paid tribute to Monfils for the way he responded to her decision, saying he had listened to her needs with dignity and understanding.“Gaël loved me in both the happiest and the darkest moments of my life. And I loved him with all my heart,” she added.Daughter Skai remains their priorityDespite confirming the end of their marriage, Svitolina stressed that their responsibilities as parents would remain unchanged. The couple share a daughter, Skai, who they said would continue to be their foremost priority.“Together, we built a beautiful life, and we were given the most precious gift of all, our daughter, Skai,” Svitolina wrote.“Skai will always come first. Our marriage is ending, but our family is not. We will always be her parents, side by side, at every step of her life.”The Ukrainian also made it clear that neither partner should be blamed for the separation, describing it as a difficult personal decision rather than the result of wrongdoing by either individual.“There are only two people who deeply loved each other, and a story that is now taking a different form,” she wrote, asking the public to respect their privacy as they navigate the transition.“We ask you to treat us with kindness and give us the privacy and time we need to heal. Thank you for your love.”Monfils' retirement adds another chapterThe announcement comes amid a significant transition in Monfils' tennis career. The 40-year-old Frenchman had planned to retire at the end of the 2026 season, with a farewell appearance at the Paris Masters expected to be a fitting conclusion in front of his home crowd.However, the sport’s drug-testing organisation has listed Monfils among players who have declared themselves retired, with his career officially ending on October 5.Monfils, a former world No. 6, enjoyed a long career marked by his athleticism and showmanship, while Svitolina has established herself among the leading players on the women’s tour.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi won 30 Grand Slam titles combined, but never expected their kids to follow their legacy: Here’s why the sporting legends chose to give the kids freedom to explore their own passions and enjoy childhood without the pressure
articles.summary: Tennis champions Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi built extraordinary careers, winning 30 Grand Slam singles titles between them.
articles.body: Tennis champions Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi built extraordinary careers, winning 30 Grand Slam singles titles between them. But when it came to raising their children, Jaden Gil Agassi and Jaz Elle Agassi, they made a different choice. They did not expect their children to follow their footsteps into tennis. Instead, they wanted them to enjoy something their own childhoods had often lacked: the freedom to discover who they were.Andre Agassi knew what it meant to lose a childhoodAgassi's relationship with tennis began long before he could make an informed choice about his future. His father, Mike Agassi, pushed him into the sport from an early age, expecting him to become a champion.In his autobiography Open, Agassi described his complicated relationship with tennis. Despite his success, he wrote about the loneliness and emotional strain of competing, calling it the loneliest sport possible.Also Read: Paul McCartney’s daughter Beatrice reportedly wanted to become a marine biologist rather than follow her father into music: Here's why allowing children to explore their own interests, instead of inheriting a parent’s ambitions, can help them find their path in lifeHis experience offers an important parenting lesson. A child can become exceptionally good at something without necessarily enjoying the journey. Achievement may bring trophies and recognition, but it cannot replace the freedom to choose.Why their children did not have to inherit their legacyFor children born to sporting legends, expectations can arrive before they understand what those expectations mean. Every interest can become a potential career, and every achievement can invite comparisons with their famous parents.Graf and Agassi wanted to protect their children from that pressure. Rather than making tennis the centre of family life, they allowed Jaden and Jaz to explore interests of their own.Agassi summed up his approach with a memorable thought: "I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children's childhood."The sentiment reflects a powerful distinction between giving children opportunities and deciding their future for them.Jaden Agassi found his own sporting pathBorn in 2001, Jaden explored different sports, including soccer, before developing a passion for baseball.His journey eventually took him to the University of Southern California, where he played baseball as a pitcher. He also represented Germany in international baseball, including World Baseball Classic qualifying competition.His choice is particularly striking given his parents' achievements. Jaden did not need to become another tennis champion to pursue competitive sport seriously. He could build his own identity in a different arena.Jaz Agassi was free to explore different interestsBorn in 2003, Jaz Elle Agassi has largely kept her life private. Her interests have included dancing, horseback riding and snowboarding.Unlike her parents, she has not built a public tennis career. That difference should not be mistaken for a lack of ambition. Children do not have to pursue a high-profile profession to lead meaningful lives.Sometimes, the real privilege is being allowed to explore interests without having every hobby treated as a future career.The parenting lesson behind their decisionThe story of Graf and Agassi challenges a familiar belief: that children should continue what their parents started.A parent's experience can offer guidance, but it should not become a script that a child must follow. Even well-intentioned pressure can make an activity feel like an obligation rather than a source of joy.Graf and Agassi's approach does not mean keeping children away from parental interests. It means introducing possibilities without making acceptance conditional on choosing them.Their legacy, then, extends beyond tennis. It is also a reminder that successful parenting is not about raising a smaller version of oneself. It is about helping a child become a person of their own.Also read: Tom Selleck’s daughter Hannah Selleck left a conventional career in PR to follow her passion for horses: How growing up on a ranch, building her own business and overcoming a serious injury helped her discover her identity beyond her famous familyDisclaimer: This article draws on publicly reported information about the Agassi-Graf family and their sporting careers.You use AI every day. articles.title: Elina Svitolina announces 'difficult' separation from husband Gael Monfils after five years of marriage
articles.summary: Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils have announced their separation; The tennis players married in 2021 and have a four-year-old daughter; Watch the Japan Open all this week, live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
In an emotional Instagram post, the 32-year-old Ukrainian opened up about the mental toll of Russia's ongoing war against her country, describing sleepless nights and self-doubt.

Svitolina said she had come to realise she needed to rediscover herself and could no longer do so within her marriage. "This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share," she wrote.

"Everyone knows how much Ukraine means to me. What I have rarely spoken about is what the war has done to me inside.

"With time, I came to understand that I need to find my way back to myself and that I cannot do that within our marriage.

"It is the hardest truth I have ever had to face and the hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love. Gael listened. He has respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget."

Svitolina - a four-time grand slam semi-finalist - and French former world No 6 Monfils, 40, married in 2021 and have a four-year-old daughter, Skai.

"Skai will always come first," Svitolina added. "Our marriage is ending, but our family is not.

"Please know that there is no one to blame here. There are only two people who loved each other deeply and a story that is changing shape."

Only a few months ago Svitolina and Monfils had joined forces to reach the semi-finals of the US Open Mixed Doubles Championship.

Svitolina and Monfils had impressed in the tournament until coming up against Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli in the last four.

More recently, Svitolina was in action at the Wuhun Open, but ran into an inspired Sonay Kartal, with the Brit winning their quarter-final clash in three sets.

articles.title: Japan Open: Katie Boulter puts rain delays behind her as Brit progresses to second round in Osaka
articles.summary: Britain's Katie Boulter books place in second round of Japan Open, after defeating home wildcard Himeno Sakatsume; Play had been suspended the day before due to heavy rainfall in Osaka; Watch the Japan Open all this week, live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
The world No 58 concluded a dominant victory in one hour and 32 minutes in Osaka, and she will next face Swiss player Viktorija Golubic for a place in the quarter-finals.

The victory gives Boulter a 20-20 record across her last 40 matches, and a confidence boost following a period in which she has only played three matches since September 30, owing to early exits at the China Open (second round) and Wuhan Open (first round).

On Monday, the match between Boulter and Sakatsume had barely started when the players were forced off court after torrential rain arrived in Osaka. Given the venue didn't have a roof, the court was open to all of the elements.

By that point, only three games had been played in the first set, with Sakatsume leading 2-1 at the time of the suspension.

Play was resumed, but another rain delay followed with the score 6-3 3-1 (40-30) to Boulter, meaning both players had to leave court and return on Tuesday to finish the contest.

When play restarted again, 30-year-old Boulter continued to dominate, winning seven of her eight service games overall and claiming five of nine break point chances.

Swiatek withdraws from Ningbo Open with left thigh injury

Elsewhere, Iga Swiatek has withdrawn from the Ningbo Open in China because of an injured left thigh, diminishing her chances of contesting the season-ending WTA Finals at Indian Wells next month.

The six-time major winner lost to eventual champion Maja Chwalinska in the semi-finals at the Wuhan Open last week and struggled at times in that match.

"After careful consideration, I've decided to withdraw from the tournament," Swiatek said in a statement posted on social media Tuesday by the Ningbo tournament. "I've been experiencing an ongoing problem with my left thigh over the past weeks and I feel that giving myself the time to rest and recover is the right decision."

Swiatek was one of three players in contention for the last spot in the eight-player field for the WTA Finals with Karolina Muchova and Marta Kostyuk ahead of tournaments this week.

The WTA, in a preview of the Ningbo tournament, said if Swiatek didn't reach the quarter-finals and Kostyuk doesn't reach the final here, Muchova will secure the remaining spot for the season-ending tournament at Indian Wells starting November 8.

articles.title: Tennis star Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation
articles.summary: The two top tennis pros married in 2021 and have one child together.
articles.body:
Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced the end of her marriage with French former tennis player Gaël Monfils, citing the emotional impact of the war in her country.

The 32-year-old, who is ranked number six in the world, wrote in a heartfelt post on Instagram about the effect the conflict and "what the war has done to me inside".

"This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share," she wrote, saying "I need to find my way back to myself". Svitolina said she felt she could not do that within her marriage.

She said her husband Monfils, 40, "listened" and "respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget".

"Some battles happen deep inside you, and no amount of love from someone else can win them for you," the four-time Grand Slam semi-finalist wrote.

It was "the hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love", Svitolina said.

"Everyone knows how much Ukraine means to me," Svitolina, who grew up in Odesa, said.

Ukraine's Black Sea port city has been heavily bombed by Russia throughout the war.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

"What you didn't see were the sleepless nights, the doubts, and the feeling of slowly losing myself."

The tennis power couple married in 2021 and have one child together - a four-year-old daughter called Skai.

Svitolina said her daughter "will always come first", adding "our marriage is ending, but our family is not".

articles.title: Munar supera al 'qualy' Cina y se mete en octavos del torneo de Bruselas
articles.standfirst: El mallorquín es el único español en el certamen belga de categoría 250
articles.summary: El mallorquín es el único español en el certamen belga de categoría 250
articles.body: Jaume Munar, el 51 del ranking ATP a sus 29 años, se ha clasificado este lunes para los octavos del Open 250 de Bruselas. El mallorquín acabó con la resistencia del prometedor italiano Federico Cina, procedente de la previa, por 6-4 y 6-3. Munar se verá las caras en la segunda ronda con Arthur Fils, número 10 de las listas y el primer favorito del certamen. Fils está exento de la ronda inicial y busca puntos para acercarse al objetivo de las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre). Es rival directo de Rafa Jódar y Alejandro Davidovich por una de las cinco plazas restantes en la cita de maestros. Están matemáticamente clasificados Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz y Ben Shelton. En el caso de Jannik Sinner, también con billete directo, causará baja por su lesión de rodilla. Munar es el único miembro de la 'Armada' en tierras belgas. No hay ninguno en Almaty y Martín Landaluce es la raqueta nacional en el torneo de Lyon. El madrileño, que viene de perder la final del challenger de Jinan (China) con Mattia Bellucci, jugará su primer partido con el invitado Stan Wawrinka. El suizo, de 41 años, cuelga la raqueta a finales de la presente temporada.

articles.title: Cristina Bucsa, la representante española en las WTA Finals de dobles
articles.standfirst: La tenista de Torrelavega está completando una gran temporada con Nicole Melichar
articles.summary: La tenista de Torrelavega está completando una gran temporada con Nicole Melichar
articles.body: El tenis femenino español tendrá representación en las WTA Finals de Indian Wells (8 al 15 de noviembre). Además de Garbiñe Muguruza, que será la directora del torneo de maestras, habrá una raqueta nacional en la pista compitiendo. Se trata de Cristina Bucsa, que se ha clasificado en la modalidad del dobles formando pareja con Nicole Melichar. Bucsa participará en las WTA Finals por primera vez. Será la quinta para Melichar-Martinez, que tiene como mejor resultado la final de 2023. La pareja formada entre la española y la estadounidense conquistaron el 500 de Guadalajara. Otros resultados destacados fueron la final del WTA 1000 de Roma y las semifinales en el BNP Paribas Open (Indian Wells), precisamente la ubicación de la cita de maestras en 2026 sustituyendo a Riad.

articles.title: Tennis power-couple Elina Svitolina and Gaël Monfils split: Inside their combined net worth, career earnings and endorsements after five years of marriage
articles.summary: Elina Svitolina and Gaël Monfils have split after five years of marriage. Discover their journey from romance to parenthood, their combined net worth, career achievements, and how they plan to navigate co-parenting after their separation.
articles.body: Elina Svitolina and Gaël Monfils built one of tennis’s most recognisable relationships while establishing successful careers on opposite sides of the sport. Their marriage, which began in 2021, has now come to an end, with Svitolina announcing their separation in an emotional Instagram post. The news has brought renewed attention to their life together, including the fortune they accumulated through years on tour, sponsorships and investments.How the tennis stars met, married and became parentsAlthough they had crossed paths on the professional circuit, Monfils and Svitolina’s relationship began in 2018, when he invited her to join him and friends for drinks after she won the WTA Finals in Singapore. They began dating and later announced their engagement on Instagram on April 3, 2021, showing Svitolina’s three-stone emerald-cut ring against a snow-covered mountain backdrop.The pair married in July 2021 and welcomed their daughter, Skaï, the following year. Svitolina returned to competitive tennis not long after becoming a mother, balancing family life with the demands of the tour.Their careers continued to produce notable milestones together. In 2026, Svitolina won the ASB Classic women’s singles title in Auckland, matching Monfils’ 2025 men’s singles triumph there and making them one of the few married couples to win singles titles at the same tournament in consecutive years.Elina Svitolina and Gaël Monfils’ net worth and career earningsThe couple’s combined net worth in 2026 has been estimated at around $40–42 million, although those figures are not independently verified and should be treated as estimates. Their wealth reflects long careers at the highest level, with prize money providing a substantial foundation and endorsements adding to their earnings.CategoryElina SvitolinaGaël MonfilsCombinedEstimated Net Worth (2026)$18–20 Million$20–22 Million$40–42 MillionGrand Slam Titles000Career Prize Money$25M+$24.5M+$49.5M+Major EndorsementsWilson, Rolex, AdidasWilson, Asics, SponsorsMultiple DealsMain InvestmentsReal Estate, PhilanthropyReal Estate, Business InterestsShared AssetsSvitolina has earned more than $25 million in WTA prize money, while Monfils has collected more than $24.4 million on the ATP Tour. Their endorsement portfolios have included established sports and luxury brands, with Svitolina associated with Wilson, Rolex and Adidas, and Monfils with Wilson, Asics and other sponsors.Endorsements, investments and the fortune beyond tennisPrize money has been central to the couple’s estimated wealth, but sponsorships and commercial opportunities have also contributed. Their visibility, distinctive playing styles and large social-media followings made them attractive to brands, while their careers gave them opportunities to plan financially beyond tournament earnings.Neither has been widely associated with a sprawling business empire, though the supplied estimates list real estate and other business interests among their investments. Reports in 2025 also referred to their backing of a free community-facility initiative valued at around £3 million, reflecting a philanthropic dimension to their public lives.Their financial position is not a public accounting of assets, liabilities or how property and investments are divided. The combined estimate therefore describes their reported wealth during their marriage, not a confirmed assessment of either person’s individual finances following the separation.Svitolina announces the end of their marriageOn Instagram, Svitolina described announcing the separation as “the most difficult thing I have ever had to share.” She said the psychological toll of the war in Ukraine had affected her mental and emotional well-being over the past year, bringing sleepless nights, self-doubt and a feeling that she was losing herself.She also acknowledged Monfils’ support during that period, writing, “He never let go of my hand.” But Svitolina said she needed to pursue personal healing outside the marriage, explaining: “No amount of love from someone else can win them for you.”She made clear that the separation did not end their commitment to their daughter. “Our marriage is ending, but our family is not,” she wrote, adding that Skaï would remain their priority and asking the public to respect their privacy rather than assign blame.The announcement comes as Monfils prepares to leave professional tennis. In October 2025, he said on Instagram that the 2026 season would be his last, thanking those who had supported him, including Svitolina, whom he called his “love, inspiration, and strength,” and their daughter. He has reportedly been listed as retired by the sport’s drug-testing organisation, with his career ending on October 5, 2026.Their marriage is now over, but the careers, earnings and family they built together remain part of both players’ stories.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Marion Bartoli net worth 2026: Inside the former Wimbledon champion’s career, earnings, family, parents and more
articles.summary: Marion Bartoli is a former French professional tennis player. She made history with her remarkable performances on the WTA Tour.
articles.body: Marion Bartoli is a former French professional tennis player. She made history with her remarkable performances on the WTA Tour. She reached the Wimbledon final twice and won the prestigious singles title in 2013.Bartoli enjoyed a career spanning more than a decade before retiring shortly after her biggest achievement. She later explored television and tennis commentary. She also made a mark in fashion. Her Grand Slam success and consistent performances helped establish her legacy in professional tennis.Marion Bartoli’s net worth in 2026 Marion Bartoli has an estimated net worth of $6 million (per celebrity net worth). The former French tennis star built much of her wealth through tournament prize money, sponsorships and endorsements. According to official WTA career statistics, she earned approximately $11.1 million in prize money during her playing career.Her biggest achievement came at Wimbledon in 2013. Bartoli defeated Germany’s Sabine Lisicki 6-1, 6-4 in the final to win her first Grand Slam singles title. She completed the tournament without dropping a set. The victory marked the highlight of her professional career.Bartoli earned money from several other tournaments throughout her career. She won eight WTA singles titles and three doubles titles. Her consistent performances at major events also helped her secure endorsement deals. She also bagged equipment partnerships. After retiring, she continued earning through tennis commentary. This came along with television appearances and media projects.Marion's father Walter Bartoli, was a doctor, while her mother, Sophie, worked as a nurse.Her father played a major role in developing her tennis career. He coached her from a young age and designed training exercises to improve her coordination and reactions. Bartoli eventually developed a distinctive playing style. She used two hands on both her forehand and backhand, which made her stand out from other players.Her breakthrough at a Grand Slam tournament came at Wimbledon in 2007. Bartoli defeated world No. 1 Justine Henin in the semifinals to reach her first major final. However, she lost to Venus Williams in the championship match.Bartoli continued to deliver strong performances in the following years. She reached the semifinals of the 2011 French Open and the final at Indian Wells that same year. She also reached the quarterfinals of the Australian Open and the US Open.Her career-high singles ranking was No. 7 in the world. These achievements established her as one of the leading French players of her generation.Retirement and life beyond tennisBartoli announced her retirement in August 2013, shortly after winning Wimbledon. She cited injuries and the physical demands of professional tennis as reasons for her decision.Following retirement, she worked as a tennis commentator and analyst for major broadcasters. Her experience as a Grand Slam champion gave her valuable insight into professional matches. She also explored fashion and other media opportunities.In late 2017, Bartoli announced an attempt to return to professional tennis. However, she did not make a full-time comeback to the WTA Tour.In her personal life, Bartoli married Belgian footballer Yahya Boumediene in 2019. The couple welcomed a daughter in 2020.Bartoli remains best known for her historic Wimbledon triumph.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: India's Bhavina Patel and Sonalben Patel won bronze medals in women's singles table tennis at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Tuesday.
articles.body: India's Bhavina Patel and Sonalben Patel won bronze medals in women's singles table tennis at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Tuesday. Both players lost their respective semi-final matches but finished on the podium.Bhavina lost 7-11, 5-11, 7-11 to China's Zhang Bian in the Class 4-5 semi-final. Sonalben went down 7-11, 5-11, 6-11 against South Korea's Jiyu Yoon in the Class 3 semi-final.Bhavina Patel wins second successive bronzeBhavina, a former Paralympics silver medallist and Commonwealth Games gold medallist, suffered a straight-games defeat against Zhang, an eight-time Paralympic gold medallist.The 39-year-old from Gujarat won silver at the 2018 Asian Para Games and bronze at the 2022 edition. Her latest medal gives her a second successive bronze at the continental event.Zhang, 40, had won silver at the previous Asian Para Games.The Class 4-5 category is for wheelchair athletes with lower-limb impairments who have good upper-body control.Sonalben Patel goes down to defending championSonalben could not get past defending champion Jiyu Yoon in the Class 3 semi-final. The South Korean, a three-time Paralympic medallist, won the match in straight games.Sonalben had earlier won silver in doubles at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta.The Class 3 category is for wheelchair athletes who have limited trunk control and poor sitting balance but normal or near-normal arm and hand function.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Toni Nadal: "A Rafa le apetecerá ser capitán de la Copa Davis"
articles.standfirst: "No sé en qué momento, pero supongo que sí que le apetecería y ya le tocará. Además Rafa es de los que hace grupo"
articles.summary: "No sé en qué momento, pero supongo que sí que le apetecería y ya le tocará. Además Rafa es de los que hace grupo"
articles.body: Toni Nadal, tío y antiguo entrenador de Rafa Nadal, habló en el programa 'Radioestadio Noche' sobre el equipo de Copa Davis de España después de que David Ferrer anunciase que dejaba la capitanía a final de temporada. "Conozco a David Ferrer, como persona es un 10 y la decisión que tome será por el bien del equipo español", comentó Toni Nadal. Joan Solsona informa en MARCA que Marc López será el nuevo seleccionador de la Copa Davis a partir de 2027 y hasta 2029 como sustituto de David Ferrer. El barcelonés, segundo de Ferrer desde el año pasado en la capitanía, tomará las riendas de las selección nacional tras la fase final de Bolonia (24 a 29 de noviembre). "Marc López es una bellísima persona y se lleva bien con todo el mundo; sabe mucho de tenis". Toni Nadal destacó en Onda Cero que "la capitanía de la Copa de Davis es casi un premio a la carrera de estos grandes jugadores que se lo merecen y tiene que ser más o menos rotativa". "Los jugadores se rebotan menos cuando más grande o más nombre tiene el capitán", apuntó. Toni Nadal también habló sobre un hipotético futuro de Rafa Nadal como capitán de la Copa Davis. "Creo y digo que a Rafa le apetecerá ser capitán de la Davis, no sé en qué momento, pero supongo que sí que le apetecería y ya le tocará. Además Rafa es de los que hace grupo", reconoció el Director y Embajador de la Rafa Nadal Academy.

articles.title: La tenista Eva Lys cierra su temporada para centrase en su "salud física y mental"
articles.standfirst: "Ha sido uno de los años más duros de mi vida, tanto dentro como fuera de la pista"
articles.summary: "Ha sido uno de los años más duros de mi vida, tanto dentro como fuera de la pista"
articles.body: Eva Lys ha decidido anticipar el final de su temporada 2026 con el objetivo de "centrarme en mi salud física y mental" y encontrar su mejor versión de cara a 2007. La tenista alemana de 24 años, que empezó la temporada en el puesto 39 del ranking WTA y actualmente ocupa el puesto 136, ha vivido una temporada especialmente complicada en la que su lucha contra la artritis ha afectado tanto a su rendimiento como a su vida cotidiana. "Ha sido uno de los años más duros de mi vida, tanto dentro como fuera de la pista", confesó Eva Lys, que esta temporada suma 8 victorias en 27 partidos, en un mensaje publicado en sus redes sociales. La tenista alemana explicó que afrontó el año con grandes expectativas, objetivos ambiciosos y mucha ilusión, pero la realidad resultó ser muy distinta. "Ha sido frustrante, agotador y, a veces, muy difícil de aceptar; sobre todo cuando te esfuerzas tanto por algo y tu cuerpo y tu mente simplemente no colaboran". Eva Lys desveló que "gran parte de esto se debe a mi lucha constante contra la artritis, que este año ha sido especialmente difícil de sobrellevar. Después de más de seis años, hemos decidido dar un paso importante y cambiar mi tratamiento. Es un ajuste grande que requerirá tiempo, pero confío en que es un paso en la dirección correcta.". "Sean amables, sigan su propio camino y no se apresuren a juzgar a los demás. Nunca se sabe realmente qué es lo que ocurre entre bastidores. Y a todos los que se han quedado a mi lado, me han apoyado y han seguido creyendo en mí a través de todos los altibajos: gracias. Los valoro más de lo que imaginan", apuntó. Eva Lys compartió que "me tomaré el tiempo necesario para recuperar mi salud. Espero con ganas el 2027 y todo lo que traiga consigo. Volveré".

articles.title: Andrey Rublev opens up on mental struggles, says 'I was at the bottom of my darkest days'
articles.summary: ALMATY: Andrey Rublev has spent much of his career trying to get better at being Andrey Rublev.
articles.body: ALMATY: Andrey Rublev has spent much of his career trying to get better at being Andrey Rublev. Now, the mercurial Russian, whose on-court meltdowns are almost as well chronicled as his title wins, is attempting to rewrite the script that took him to world No. 5.At 28, he is trying to become a different player. Rublev has slipped to No. 22, falling outside the top 20 for the first time since Jan 2020. For a player who finished each season inside the top 10 from 2020 to 2024, the decline is striking.Yet, after 10 Grand Slam quarterfinal appearances without advancing to a semifinal, Rublev has come to a realisation — to build something new, he must first be willing to break down what got him here.“It’s not easy to change something that you know for all your life,” said Rublev, the No. 4 seed at the Almaty Open, an ATP 250 event. “It’s not easy to switch that, what brought you to No. 5 in the world for something else that you don’t really trust yet.”The forehand, Rublev’s biggest weapon, is a useful example. It’s a shot he could turn to under pressure almost without thinking.“I’m trying to change, on and off the court, mentally, things that have become a habit, that have already taken me to the limit, with what I could do with that,” he says, eyes fixed on the table before him. “Now, it’s the second part of (my) career where I try to do something different completely.”There is no guarantee the experiment will work. Rublev knows that as well as anyone.“Maybe it’s going to make the second part of my career better than my first part, or maybe not,” he says, lifting his gaze. “But at least I know I did something, I gave myself a chance.”“With the game I used to have, it will go down little by little until I cannot play anymore,” he says. “To be just top 30 for the next five-six years, for me, it makes no difference.”For the past 18 months, Rublev has been working with former world No. 1 Marat Safin, a partnership that has pushed the 28-year-old to address mental and emotional struggles that have led him to hurt himself physically on court.Asked what has changed most since working with Safin, Rublev does not begin with tactics or results.“I’m enjoying much more the life. I’m much more in peace with myself,” he says.It is a striking answer from a player whose intensity has long been one of the defining features of his tennis.“From the past, before Marat, I was very depressed, and taking antidepressant pills to not feel depression,” he says.He pauses, taking a deep breath, before describing how low he had felt.“Basically, it was a bit of drama that was happening to me, and I didn’t know how to escape. I was at the bottom of my darkest days.”It was there, he says, that he reached a point at which he could no longer continue as he had been. He faced a choice, to remain trapped in the same patterns or to try, finally, to do something about them.“I choose to try to fix it,” he said.Rublev is not short of reminders that reinvention is possible.“When you see players like Sasha (Zverev) or Daniil (Medvedev), when they're doing something good, it gives a clear signal that I can do it as well,” he says. “Because I know what I'm capable of. If he can do it, I can find a way as well.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Paula Badosa pierde su primer partido tras romper con Pol Toledo
articles.standfirst: Antonia Ruzic dio la vuelta a la ventaja inicial de Paula Badosa y ganó por 3-6, 6-4 y 6-3 en el torneo de Osaka de categoría 250
articles.summary: Antonia Ruzic dio la vuelta a la ventaja inicial de Paula Badosa y ganó por 3-6, 6-4 y 6-3 en el torneo de Osaka de categoría 250
articles.body: En su primer partido sin Pol Toledo como entrenador, con el que rompió la semana pasada, la española Paula Badosa fue superada en su puesta en escena en el torneo de Osaka, de categoría 250, vencida por la croata Antonia Ruzic. La balcánica dio la vuelta a la ventaja inicial de la jugadora española y ganó por 3-6, 6-4 y 6-3 para situarse en la segunda ronda del evento nipón, después de dos horas y veinticuatro minutos. Es la segunda derrota seguida de Paula Badosa, que en el torneo WTA 1000 de Pekín no superó el segundo tramo y después de vencer a la australiana Daria Kasatkina cayó ante la letona Jelena Ostapenko. El encuentro ante Ruzic, a la que había ganado en el único duelo previo ante ambas, en Pekín el pasado curso, fue el primero que Badosa disputó sin Pol Toledo en su palco. La semana pasada, la jugadora catalana rompió con el que ha sido su entrenador hace casi cuatro años. Paula Badosa, 58 de la clasificación mundial, tiene a la vista ahora los torneos de Guangzhou y Hong Kong, ya en noviembre. Ruzic, 93 del ránking, se enfrentará en segunda ronda a la ganadora del duelo entre las estadounidenses Kayla Day y Sofia Kenin.

articles.title: ‘I’m playing better now’: Stefanos Tsitsipas on father-coach split, pressure and his tennis revival
articles.summary: ALMATY: Stefanos Tsitsipas folded his 6 ft 4’ frame into a sofa in a busy corridor at the Almaty Open. The 28-year-old, once ranked as high as No.
articles.body: ALMATY: Stefanos Tsitsipas folded his 6 ft 4’ frame into a sofa in a busy corridor at the Almaty Open.The 28-year-old, once ranked as high as No. 3 in the world and now at No. 39, acknowledged that his road back began with letting go. Letting go of the pressure, the tension and the expectations that have weighed on him. And, most importantly, allowing his father to be a father again, rather than having to be both father and coach.Tsitsipas, who finished in the Top-10 for five consecutive years, from 2019 to 2023, believes he is playing better tennis now than he was a few years ago, when he reached two Grand Slam finals, at Roland Garros in 2021 and the Australian Open in 2023.The dip in form began with his body, a back problem that had been troubling him for some time, compounded by a strained coaching relationship with his father, Apostolos. The combination took its toll on his confidence, and by June his ranking had plummeted to No. 88.Just before Wimbledon, Tsitsipas told Greek media that he was ending his professional relationship with his father for good.“I love my father, and I love him as a father,” he said in Almaty. “I want to keep the professional part out of my relationship with my father. My relationship with him has improved now that he’s not my coach. It was very difficult for me to separate the coach and the father. I had reached a point where I could not avoid being triggered.”“We’re still in touch, and I really like the way things are right now,” he added.That separation appears to have given Tsitsipas something he had been missing, room to breathe. The weight of expectation and the tension of a relationship complicated by professional demands had produced disturbing scenes at tennis tournaments around the world, a father in his fifties hurling instructions at his son, sometimes leading to heated exchanges between the two.“Eliminating the pressure factor does help,” he told TOI at the Almaty Open. “Before, I felt pressured a lot of the time. There were a lot of things piled up within me, and certain people triggered me in a negative way. Removing some of those triggers, and having people around me who keep me calm and help me be more forgiving (on myself) when things don't work out, allows me to experiment more and not be afraid to try things.”For Tsitsipas, that freedom is essential for growth.“When you feel judged, you tend to go for the safe options. And safety is not always where growth is. You need a team that isn't going to judge you for what you do, but will analyse it and support you, because it's all part of the process.”The numbers suggest that the process is beginning to pay off. Across his first 16 events of the season, Tsitsipas went 16-14. In the 10 tournaments since Wimbledon, he has gone 21-8, winning the title in Gstaad in July to end a 16-month drought.Now working with Thomas Perrin, and with Patrick Mouratoglou overseeing the process, he believes his tennis is better than it has been in years.“I'm playing better now than I played a few years back,” he said.“I feel like I was kind of stuck in the past. Certain aspects of my game weren't properly structured, and there wasn't really a base to build on.”Since August, he has beaten Arthur Fils, No. 11 (then ranked), Jiri Lehecka, No. 19, Tomas Etcheverry, No. 30, Luciano Darderi 21, and Taylor Fritz, No. 12.One of the most revealing signs of that progress concerns his backhand. One of only three players in the top 50 to use a single-handed backhand, alongside Lorenzo Musetti and Denis Shapovalov, Tsitsipas has increasingly found opponents targeting that side of the court.“My backhand is probably even better than my forehand right now. I've played some really good matches and used it as an actual weapon on court. Against (Daniil) Medvedev recently, I used it to approach the net, slice, change pace and rhythm, play down the line and open up the court. There's more variety now, whereas before it felt like one-way traffic.”Range matters. Tsitsipas knows opponents will continue to target his backhand, but he feels better equipped to respond, using changes of pace, depth and direction to keep them guessing rather than allowing them to dictate play.For Tsitsipas, the way forward is about rediscovering the freedom to play on his own terms, with a clearer mind and a game he believes in again.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Katie Boulter produces emphatic win at Japan Open
articles.summary: Britain's Katie Boulter claims a dominant win in her rain-affected first-round match against Himeno Sakatsume in the Japan Open.
articles.body:
Katie Boulter claimed a dominant win in her rain-affected first round match against Himeno Sakatsume in the Japan Open.

The British player was a set and 3-1 up against the home favourite when play was halted because of bad weather in Osaka on Monday.

She completed the win on Tuesday as she secured a 6-3 6-1 victory.

"Yesterday was a tough spot to end at," said Boulter, who will play Viktorija Golubic of Switzerland in the second round.

"I wanted to play last night and continue but with the rain, unfortunately, that wasn't possible.

"It meant that I had to have the same mindset again today and just try to get over the line and focus on getting through the match.

"I think I did that. I didn't want to be out here playing a third set so I'm pleased with today."

Boulter, 30, took five of nine break points in the match and, even though she faced 13 break points, wild card Sakatsume only managed to take one.

Meanwhile, Iga Swiatek's hopes of reaching the WTA Finals in Indian Wells have suffered a setback with the world number nine having withdrawn from the Ningbo Open because of a thigh injury.

The Finals, which feature the top eight singles players and doubles teams of the year, is taking place from 8-15 November.

articles.title: Katie Boulter advances after rain delays at Japan Open as Iga Swiatek fails to qualify for WTA Finals
articles.summary: Boulter bounced back from a first-round defeat in Wuhan to defeat the Japanese wildcard
articles.body:
Katie Boulter is through to the second round of the Japan Open after overcoming a rain delay to win in straight sets against home favourite Himeno Sakatsume.

Boulter led by a set and by 3-1 in the second set when play was suspended on Monday as a result of poor weather in Osaka.

But she picked up where she left off when play resumed on Tuesday, winning 6-3 6-1 to set up a second-round meeting with Switzerland's Viktorija Golubic.

She said: "Yesterday was a tough spot to end at. I wanted to play last night and continue but with the rain, unfortunately, that wasn't possible. It meant that I had to have the same mindset again today and just try to get over the line and focus on getting through the match.

"I think I did that. I didn't want to be out here playing a third set so I'm pleased with today."

Boulter, who has been replaced by Sonay Kartal as British No 1 after the 24-year-old's brilliant run to the Wuhan Open final, saved 12 of 13 break points against the Japanese wildcard as she bounced back from a first-round defeat in Wuhan.

Elsewhere Iga Swiatek is set to miss out on the WTA Finals for the first time since 2020 after she withdrew from the Ningbo Open due to a thigh injury.

The six-time grand slam champion was hampered by the injury during her semi-final defeat to compatriot and eventual champion Maja Chwalinska in Wuhan last week.

The Pole, who won the season-ending Finals in 2023, needed to reach at least the quarter-finals in Ningbo in order to keep her chances of qualifying for the tournament alive, although she could still make the cut to travel there as one of two alternates.

She sits ninth in the rankings race for the event in Indian Wells , which is determined by points totals over the course of the season. Karolina Muchova , who is also not competing at the WTA 500 tournament in Ningbo, and Marta Kostyuk are vying for the final spot.

articles.title: Alcaraz regresa a los entrenamientos y viaja este sábado a Viena
articles.standfirst: El murciano vuelve a la competición el próximo martes, 15 días después de caer con Bergs en Shanghái
articles.summary: El murciano regresará a la competición el próximo martes, 15 días después de caer con Bergs en Shanghái
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ya ha fijado su hoja de ruta para lo que resta de temporada. Después de su derrota ante Zizou Bergs en la tercera ronda del Masters 1000 de Shanghái, el murciano se tomó unos días libres antes de su regreso a los entrenamientos con la vista puesta en el Open 500 de Viena. El tenista pidió una invitación a la organización una vez cancelado el Six Kings Slam de Riad, que debía disputar esta semana del 21 al 24. Alcaraz, que volverá a jugar en la capital austriaca cinco años después, será el segundo cabeza de serie ya que el primero es Alexander Zverev, número dos mundial y que se ha asegurado acabar el curso por delante de los demás. Según ha podido saber MARCA, Alcaraz y su equipo partirán hacia Viena este sábado para preparar el debut, que será el martes 27. Habrán pasado 15 días de la derrota con Bergs en Shanghái. El pupilo de Samuel López busca rodaje en superficie dura bajo techo donde se juegan los dos títulos más ilusionantes para él de final de curso: las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre) y la fase final de la Copa Davis (24 al 29). En la presente temporada, Carlitos apenas ha disputado un partido en dura a cubierto, con triunfo ante Taylor Fritz en la Laver Cup de Londres. Su bagaje en ese hábitat es de 36 triunfos por 15 derrotas, lo que da un porcentaje de efectividad del 70,06 por ciento, el más bajo que tiene de todas las superficies. En la lista de inscritos en Viena, además de Zverec y Alcaraz, figuran Flavio Cobolli, Daniil Medvedev, Alex de Miñaur y Frances Tiafoe (en la carrera por estar en las ATP Finals).

articles.title: Historic high! India win record five bronze medals in best-ever para table tennis show at Asian Para Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India scripted their best-ever performance in para table tennis at the Asian Para Games, securing five bronze medals in Aichi-Nagoya on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India scripted their best-ever performance in para table tennis at the Asian Para Games, securing five bronze medals in Aichi-Nagoya on Tuesday, with Ravi Baby Sahana and Prachi Pandey creating history by becoming the country's first players to win medals in the standing category at the continental showpiece.The five-medal haul took India past their previous best of two bronze medals at the last edition of the Games. Paralympics medallist Bhavina Patel and Sonalben Patel also finished on the podium after losing their respective women's singles semifinals, while Jehan Madan secured bronze in the men's singles Class 1 event.The landmark performance underlined India's growing presence in para table tennis, with medals coming across both standing and wheelchair categories.Sahana, Prachi break new ground in standing categoryTamil Nadu's Sahana went down 8-11, 2-11, 4-11 to China's Mao Jingdian, a five-time Paralympic gold medallist, in the Class 9 semifinal.Prachi, who has a neurodegenerative disease, lost 9-11, 2-11, 8-11 to Iraq's reigning Paralympic champion Najlah Al-Dayyeni in the Class 6 last-four clash.Despite their defeats, both Indians secured bronze medals and made history as the country's first para table tennis players to reach the podium in the standing category at the Asian Para Games.Class 9 is for standing athletes with physical impairments affecting their legs or playing arm, while Class 6 covers players with severe impairments affecting their arms and legs.Bhavina, Sonalben and Jehan add to India's medal haulFormer Paralympic silver medallist Bhavina lost 7-11, 5-11, 7-11 to China's eight-time Paralympic champion Zhang Bian in the Class 4-5 semifinal. The 39-year-old from Gujarat thus secured her second consecutive Asian Para Games medal after winning doubles silver in 2018. She is also a former Commonwealth Games gold medallist.Sonalben, a doubles silver medallist at the 2018 Jakarta Games, went down 7-11, 5-11, 6-11 to South Korea's defending champion Jiyu Yoon in the Class 3 semifinal.Jehan claimed bronze in the men's singles Class 1 event by virtue of finishing fourth in a five-player field. He won one of his four matches, while compatriot Sandeep Jangi finished last without a victory.India's five-bronze haul marked a significant milestone for the country's para table tennis campaign, with the historic standing-category medals adding special significance to its best-ever Asian Para Games showing.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Iga Swiatek da por finalizado un 2026 de menos a más
articles.standfirst: La polaca, con motivo de "descansar y recuperarse físicamente", cierra otro año complicado con un título en su haber
articles.summary: La polaca, con motivo de "descansar y recuperarse físicamente", cierra otro año complicado con un título en su haber
articles.body: Ya lo anunciaron esta misma semana figuras como Joao Fonseca y Eva Lys. Hoy, Iga Swiatek ha decidido poner fin a la temporada 2026. La que fuera número 1 del mundo por 125 semanas ha subido un comunicado a sus redes sociales donde da por cerrado su calendario, y no disputará ningún torneo en lo que resta de año. Esta mañana ya confirmó su baja del WTA 500 de Ningbu, lo que la deja fuera de las WTA Finals por primera vez desde 2020. En su última participación en pista salió derrotada ante su compatriota Maja Chwalinska, campeona del título en Wuhan. La polaca compitió la primera manga pero unas molestias la sacaron del encuentro. Las imagenes de Iga llorando mientras era tratada por el fisio recorrieron el circuito. En otro año complicado para Iga, donde solo ha sido capaz de levantar un certamen (WTA 1000 de Toronto), ha achacado su decisión al cansancio físico y la exigencia de la temporada: "Esta ha sido una de las temporadas más exigentes de mi carrera, llena de desafíos, cambios y aprendizajes... Los últimos meses han sido increíblemente intensos, y siento que necesito descansar y recuperar mi cuerpo por completo. Así que eso es exactamente lo que haré; esta vez, durante un periodo un poco más largo", declara la siete veces campeona de Grand Slam. Menciona el avance conseguido, sobre todo, en la segunda mitad de la temporada: "Me siento especialmente orgullosa del trabajo que hemos realizado durante la segunda mitad del año y de los avances que hemos logrado. Esto me da mucha confianza de cara a lo que viene". La polaca registra un historial de 39 victorias y 15 derrotas, aunque los momentos más duros los vivió en la gira de tierra. Algunos de estos: el abandono por enfermedad en Madrid o la derrota a manos de la ucraniana Marta Kostyuk en su querida Philippe Chatrier de París. "He decidido dar por terminada mi temporada aquí, lo que significa que no disputaré más torneos este año. Me siento agradecida por todo lo que este año me ha enseñado y sigo disfrutando muchísimo de lo que hago. Como siempre, regresaré con pasión y motivación para seguir mejorando", termina Iga, que ya mira a un próspero 2027.

articles.title: Iga Swiatek: Six-time Grand Slam champion ends 2026 season after failing to qualify for WTA Finals
articles.summary: Six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek ends her 2026 season after failing to qualify for the WTA Finals for the first time since 2019.
articles.body:
Six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek has called an early finish to what she described as "one of the most challenging" seasons of her career.

Poland's Swiatek failed to qualify for the end-of-season WTA Finals - for the first time since 2019 - after pulling out of the Ningbo Open on Tuesday with a thigh injury.

Shortly afterwards, the 25-year-old announced she was bringing a largely barren season to a close, in order to recharge over a longer period of time before returning in 2027.

Former long-time world number one Swiatek - who has ended a season without a Grand Slam title for the first time since 2021 - has dropped to ninth in the rankings.

"The past few months, or actually the past couple of years, have been incredibly intense," said Swiatek, who will have an opportunity to complete the career Grand Slam at the Australian Open in January.

"I feel I need to rest and recover my body fully, so that's exactly what I will do - [for] a bit longer this time."

Her most recent Grand Slam triumph came at Wimbledon last year.

Swiatek has managed one WTA title this season - the Canadian Open in August - and ends 2026 with a 42-16 win-loss record.

On Saturday, she lost to fellow Pole Maja Chwalinska in the Wuhan Open semi-finals, only her fourth defeat in 23 matches.

"I'm especially proud of the work we've done in the second half of the year and the progress that came with it," said Swiatek, who needed treatment on her thigh but played on against Chwalinska.

"It gives me a lot of confidence in what's ahead."

Analysis: Time for Swiatek to rest body and mind

Swiatek's decision to curtail her 2026 campaign was not a surprise once she withdrew from Ningbo.

For a player who would have automatic qualification for the WTA Finals down as a bare minimum for her yearly expectations, there seems little sense in Swiatek continuing.

Even if the injury cleared up sufficiently to play another tour event in Tokyo, or go to the season finale in Indian Wells as an alternate, she would not have got the mental break which it has long looked like she has needed.

It has been another season of flux and frustration.

In March, she split from Belgian coach Wim Fissette and soon afterwards appointed Spaniard Francisco Roig - the former coach of Rafael Nadal and Emma Raducanu - as she looked to return to being "a rock on the court".

Lifting a WTA 1,000 trophy in Toronto has been the clear high for Swiatek this year.

The unusual explosion of pent-up emotion when she beat Elena Rybakina - now the world number one - demonstrated what it meant and looked to be a turning point.

However, the stress and anxiety which she has openly spoken about feeling on the court - leading to erratic unforced errors - has not gone away.

Swiatek has often been overcome by emotion during matches, most recently when she wiped away tears during her defeat by childhood friend Chwalinska.

While that was somewhat down to the injury, Swiatek's refreshingly honest answer afterwards - that she could "go on a longer vacation" by not reaching the WTA Finals - gave a clearer indication of what she really needs before getting back to work ahead of 2027.

articles.title: La espalda obliga a Munar a retirarse de Bruselas con la Copa Davis en el horizonte
articles.standfirst: El 26 de noviembre la 'Armada' disputa su duelo de cuartos de final ante Austria
articles.summary: El 26 de noviembre la 'Armada' disputa su duelo de cuartos de final ante Austria
articles.body: Problemas para la 'Armada'. Jaume Munar, una de las posibles elecciones de David Ferrer para ocupar la quinta plaza en el equipo español, se ha visto obligado a retirarse del ATP 250 de Bruselas por problemas en la espalda. En la ronda inicial, superó con claridad al italiano Federico Cina por 6-4 y 6-3 en lo que era su primera participación en la capital belga. En principio, el español debía disputar su duelo de segunda ronda ante el francés Arthur Fils programado para el 21 de octubre en la pista central del Brussels Expo. El principal cabeza de serie del cuadro pasa directamente a cuartos de final, por décima vez en la temporada, sin haber pisado la pista. Sin conocer la gravedad de la situación de Munar, esto puede suponer un problema de cara a la elección del quinto jugador del equipo español para las finales de la Copa Davis de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre). Las opciones de David Ferrer pasan por: Jaume Munar (51), Alejandro Davidovich (13) o Dani Mérida (42). Seguramente, los tres merecedores de estar junto al resto del combinado nacional en Bolonia. Pero el contra tiempo en la espalda juega en contra del mallorquín. Como ya adelantó MARCA, el último integrante será anunciado al término del Masters 1000 de París (2 al 8 de noviembre).

articles.title: Three titles, 15 wins: Khushi Kadian makes her mark at Fenesta
articles.summary: New Delhi: There was a time when losing a tennis match left Khushi Kadian in tears and questioning her future in the sport.
articles.body: New Delhi: There was a time when losing a tennis match left Khushi Kadian in tears and questioning her future in the sport. At 13, the Rohtak girl is learning to turn setbacks into stepping stones. Her stunning triple crown at the Fenesta Open National Tennis Championship earlier this week offered the latest evidence of that transformation.“There were so many times when I wanted to give up tennis. But I told myself that I had worked so hard and had to do something," she told TOI.Across a gruelling week, Khushi won 15 consecutive matches to sweep the girls’ under-14 singles, under-16 singles and under-16 doubles titles, partnering Sanmitha Harini. She beat Siddhi Pandey 6-3, 6-2 in the under-14 final before outlasting Ranjhana Sangram 7-6 (7-3), 7-5 in a demanding under-16 singles decider. She then teamed up with Harini to clinch the doubles crown, defeating Purvi Patwa and Sangram 6-3, 6-3.The triumph was especially significant after a disappointing outing in Thailand, where she lost to China’s Li Xiaoke in the quarterfinals of the girls’ singles at the GSPDP Asian 14U Junior Championships. There were familiar thoughts of quitting, but Khushi chose to regroup.“I really wanted to win the Nationals this time, and I am happy about it,” she said, crediting her parents and coaches for their unwavering support. "One thing I have learnt and always say is, 'come on, this is your point'. And especially on my serves, I get a bit more confident that, 'yes, this is your serve and you are going to hit an ace'. I am becoming mature and understanding my game well."Once prone to tears after early-round defeats, Khushi now speaks of staying present, breathing between points and playing one point at a time. A fan of Elena Rybakina, she hopes to progress to junior Grand Slams before pursuing her bigger ambition.“I really want to do well at the Australian Open at one point of my career,” she said. “You just have to be patient, work hard and give your best, whether you win or lose.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Serena Williams’ coach has advice for Iga Swiatek after she decides to end her 2026 season early
articles.summary: Iga Swiatek’s 2026 campaign has been tumultuous to say the least. The Pole has struggled for consistency throughout the season amid coaching changes and inju...
articles.body:
Iga Swiatek's 2026 campaign has been tumultuous to say the least.

The Pole has struggled for consistency throughout the season amid coaching changes and injury concerns.

Swiatek's recent woes were compounded earlier this week as she was forced to withdraw from the Ningbo Open, meaning she could no longer qualify for the WTA Finals.

Moreover, Swiatek ended her 2026 campaign .

"This has been one of the most demanding seasons of my career, with a lot of challenges, changes and lessons along the way," the Polish star said on social media.

Rennae Stubbs, Serena Williams' coach and a former world number one in doubles, has offered some advice to the six-time major champion as she searches for fitness and form on the WTA Tour.

Rennae Stubbs says Iga Swiatek needs to learn to play more 'feel shots'

"I'd like to see her [Swiatek] implement a drop shot into her game, she used to do that when she was a young junior. I'd like to see her hit a few more high balls," the 10-time Grand Slam champion stated on The Rennae Stubbs Podcast.

"I would like her to know that she can change the pace of her ball more. Even Jess Pegula hits a flat ball, but she will throw in a moon ball every now and again. Jess will throw in a slice forehand or backhand.

"You don't see Iga hitting any slice backhands every once in a blue moon and there are certain shots where Iga has a hard time with.

"That is in the service line area, where her grip is a real problem.

"She has not learned to play feel shots and that is a big deal in tennis. [Maja] Chwalinska is beautiful in that. Throws in some junk, throws in a high ball. You have to be able to do that.

"Novak Djokovic is the perfect example. He will change the pace and hit a high ball every now and again.

"You have to be able to go to game plan B, C, D or E. And if you are game plan A, like Sabalenka's, is not working, you are going to lose."

Australian Open: lost in the quarter-finals to eventual champion Elena Rybakina

Roland Garros: lost in the fourth round to Marta Kostyuk

Wimbledon: lost in the third round to Alexandra Eala

US Open: lost in the fourth round to Qinwen Zheng

As mentioned already, it has been a season of major highs and disappointing lows for the former world number one.

The Polish superstar struggled during the first third of the campaign, leading her to part ways with coach Wim Fissette and hire Emma Raducanu's former mentor, Francisco Roig.

The highlight of Swiatek's 2026 season most definitely occurred in Toronto, where she lifted her 11th WTA 1000 title.

Swiatek defeated Marta Kostyuk, Elina Svitolina and Elena Rybakina en route to the Canadian Open title.

The Pole has suffered numerous underwhelming results since then, including losses to Elise Mertens, Maja Chwalinska and Qinwen Zheng.

The six-time Grand Slam champion will certainly hope that her 2027 WTA campaign bears more fruit.

Iga Swiatek can prove her detractors wrong immediately

When Swiatek returns to the Tour in 2027, she will have the opportunity to make tennis history almost immediately.

The Polish star is just one Australian Open title away from becoming only the 11th woman in tennis history to have completed the 'Career Grand Slam.'

The last player to accomplish the feat was Maria Sharapova, who joined the elite group following her title-winning campaign at the 2012 French Open.

Iga Swiatek's best results at Grand Slam events

Australian Open: Semi-finals [2022, 2025]

Roland Garros: CHAMPION [2020, 2022, 2023, 2024]

As for Swiatek, her best results in Australia to date occurred in 2022 and 2025: she reached the semi-finals on both occasions, losing to Danielle Collins and Madison Keys, respectively.
